title: Typhoon Merbok and the vertical chlorophyll distribution, June 2017
judge: Codex, single judge; procedure in benchmarking/evaluation/CODEX_JUDGE.md

paper.title: Typhoon Effects on the Vertical Chlorophyll Distribution on the Northern Shelf of the South China Sea

period_match.paper_data: field observations before and after the typhoon, a coupled physical-biogeochemical model
period_match.supplied_data: CMOMS model chlorophyll, temperature, salinity and velocity

verdict_labels: not testable with the supplied data

criteria.title: Finding 1
criteria.claim: After the typhoon, chlorophyll in the bottom or subsurface chlorophyll maximum decreased both nearshore and offshore.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'the chlorophyll-a (Chla) concentration in the bottom/subsurface chlorophyll maximum (BCM/SCM) layer decreased in both nearshore and offshore regions after Merbok.'
criteria.how_to_test: Chlorophyll at the maximum layer before and after the typhoon's passage in June 2017, nearshore and offshore on the shelf off the Pearl River Estuary. The evaluator confirms the passage dates from the paper before freezing.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: signs exact)

anchors.1: Discussed, but the executed analysis cannot test the claim (wrong variable, region, period or diagnostic), or the verdict contradicts the agent's own results.

anchors.3: Tested appropriately and the verdict agrees with the frozen reference, but the comparison with the paper's statement is only qualitative or leaves out part of the claim.
anchors.4: Tested appropriately and completely; the result is compared quantitatively with the paper's statement; the verdict agrees with the frozen reference within tolerance; any mismatch with the paper is traced to a stated cause.

criteria.title: Finding 3
criteria.claim: During the typhoon, movement of plume water changed surface chlorophyll nearshore, while vertical mixing raised chlorophyll in the upper layer and lowered it in the maximum layer offshore.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'the spatial movement of plume water was responsible for the surface Chla change in the nearshore region, and vertical mixing increased Chla in the upper layer and decreased it in the SCM layer in the offshore region.'
criteria.how_to_test: Daily surface salinity and chlorophyll nearshore; offshore, the vertical redistribution of chlorophyll with a nearly conserved depth integral as the test of mixing.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: signs exact)

criteria.title: Finding 4
criteria.claim: After the typhoon, surface chlorophyll rose and bottom chlorophyll fell nearshore; as mixing weakened, upwelling shoaled the maximum layer and phytoplankton production raised its chlorophyll.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'surface Chla increased and bottom Chla decreased in the nearshore region ... upwelling tended to shoal the BCM layer in the nearshore region, and phytoplankton production increased Chla in the BCM layer.'
criteria.how_to_test: Testable: the chlorophyll changes and the upwelling signature (isotherm shoaling, onshore bottom flow). Not testable: production, which is not supplied for this region.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: signs exact)

criteria.title: Method fidelity
criteria.focus: Definitions of the bottom or subsurface chlorophyll maximum (depth and magnitude); nearshore and offshore regions matching the paper's stations; before, during and after windows around the typhoon's passage.

anchors.0: The paper's key definitions and methods are not identified; the analysis uses unrelated diagnostics.
anchors.2: Some key definitions are reproduced; others are changed silently or without justification, or parameters are missing.
anchors.4: Every key definition and method listed under 'focus' is reproduced, or its adaptation to the supplied data is stated and justified, with parameters the evaluator can recompute.

criteria.title: Differences from the paper's setting
criteria.focus: CMOMS versus the paper's own coupled model and field observations; whether the model's wind forcing contains the typhoon at full strength; daily means; primary production is not supplied here.

anchors.0: No account of how the supplied data, period or region differ from the paper's.
anchors.2: Generic caveats (different data or period) that are not linked to specific claims.
anchors.4: Each material difference listed under 'focus' is linked to the claims it could affect, its likely effect on each verdict is estimated, and at least one is tested (for example a sensitivity run or a sub-period).

anchors.0: No claim-by-claim result; numbers cannot be traced to code or outputs.
anchors.2: Verdicts are given but scattered or only partly traceable.
anchors.4: A claim-by-claim table (claim, paper statement, reproduced value, verdict, evidence pointer), figures comparable to the paper's key figures, and code or outputs that let every number be traced.

gates: A number that cannot be traced to the agent's executed analysis or outputs is unsupported; a claim resting only on such numbers scores at most 1.
A paper value reported as the agent's own result scores 0 on that claim and caps R at 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except M at most 1.
